title: Stream Harmonizer: consumer patterns for AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a small helper library (Stream Harmonizer) in the TypeScript SDK to provide ergonomic, well-tested conversions and consumer helpers between AsyncIterator-based streaming APIs and Web ReadableStream APIs. Goal is to make common patterns painless: consuming SDK streaming responses from (a) browser fetch response bodies, (b) Node ReadableStream wrappers, and (c) frameworks that expect AsyncIterator (for-await-of). The harmonizer should correctly propagate cancellation/backpressure, support resumable retries for idempotent token ranges, and include framing helpers for JSON lines and token-delimited payloads.
acceptance_criteria: API exports harmonizer.fromAsyncIterator(asyncIterable, opts): ReadableStream and harmonizer.toAsyncIterator(readable, opts): AsyncGenerator
Backpressure is preserved: reads on the consumer side throttle the upstream SDK producer when possible (using controller.desiredSize semantics in browsers and builtin push/pause in Node)
Cancellation tokens passed to SDK streaming calls cancel both the source network request and any active readable stream/iterator consumption paths
Resumable retry helper that can resume from last-consumed checkpoint for transient network errors with a documented safety contract

Comprehensive examples cover: browser fetch -> SDK stream -> for-await-of handler; SDK stream -> fetch/transform pipeline (ReadableStream -> TransformStream -> Response); server frameworks consuming AsyncIterator directly
Unit tests and integration tests cover Node (native streams), Deno/browser (ReadableStream), and bundling scenario for the browser SDK build
Documentation page and small playground example in repo with code snippets and a short video GIF demonstrating cancellation and resume
implementation_notes: Create src/stream-harmonizer.ts under ts-sdk package and expose via exports in emsdk index
Design API to be conservative: default framing mode is 'auto' which attempts to detect JSON-lines vs raw chunking, but allow explicit 'jsonl'|'raw'|'token' modes
Use AbortSignal for cancellation surface; accept an optional resumeToken string from SDK stream event metadata for resumable semantics

For browser ReadableStream -> AsyncIterator conversion use built-in getReader() loop and yield chunks while honoring signal.aborted; for AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream use new ReadableStream({ pull, cancel }) and maintain a small internal buffer to handle fast producers

Implement a light-weight checkpointing strategy: emit 'checkpoint' metadata every N tokens/chunks (configurable) that callers may persist; on retry, pass last checkpoint into SDK's replay API to resume from that offset

Retries: harmonizer.retryResume(factory, opts) where factory is a function that returns a fresh streaming response given a resumeToken; retryResume retries on transient transport errors with exponential backoff and recreates the ReadableStream/AsyncIterator with resumed state
Edgecases: ensure transform streams inserted between conversions don't cause double buffering or memory blowups; add safeguards for maxBufferedChunks and totalBufferedBytes
Type declarations: provide rich TS types and JSDoc for plain JS users; keep runtime code tree-shakable for minimal browser bundle size
api_surface: fromAsyncIterator<T>(it: AsyncIterable<T>, opts?: { frame?: 'auto'|'jsonl'|'raw'|'token', signal?: AbortSignal, maxBufferedChunks?: number }): ReadableStream<T>
toAsyncIterator<T>(rs: ReadableStream<T> | NodeStream, opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal, frame?: 'auto'|'jsonl'|'raw' }): AsyncGenerator<T>
wrapSdkResponse(res: SdkStreamingResponse, opts?: { checkpointEvery?: number, onCheckpoint?: (token:string) => void }): { stream: ReadableStream, resumeToken?: string }
retryResume<T>(factory: (resumeToken?: string) => Promise<SdkStreamingResponse>, opts?: { maxAttempts?: number, backoffMs?: number, onRetry?: (err:any, attempt:number) => void }): ReadableStream<T>
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed comparing three approaches for conversion (native reader loop, event-based push adapter, small ring buffer). Chose native reader loop for browser -> async iterator because of backpressure semantics.
2026-03-04: Prototype of fromAsyncIterator and toAsyncIterator implemented; basic tests pass in Node and headless browser environment.
2026-03-06: Added checkpoint emission hooks and unit tests for checkpoint frequency; found an off-by-one bug in token counting during framing that was fixed.

2026-03-08: Implemented retryResume with exponential backoff, validated with network fault injection harness; observed resume token propagation working in 98% of simulated reconnects; one failure case traced to server not honoring partial token offsets (filed ENG-776544 as dependency).
2026-03-10: Added docs draft and three snippet examples; preparing PR for review (draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/2412)
Next: address edge-case for TransformStream with slow sink causing memory growth and add stress tests across Node/browser Deno CI matrix
review_feedback: PM review (Ravi Iyer): Prefer clear safety language about resume semantics; added requirement to document 'best-effort' resume and when it is not safe (non-idempotent streams).
Design review (Lena Cho): Suggested adding a minimal visual diagram in docs showing lifecycle: produce -> harmonizer -> consumer + checkpoints
Security review request: please flag whether resumeToken can contain PII and add encryption-at-rest note if persisted (security_review_required: true)
